Set up an editable Shiny demo for a cloud workspace

Source: R/cloud-demo.R
oauth_db_cloud_demo.Rd

Try an editable Shiny app with your own cloud workspace and account. The console guide helps you find the workspace and sign-in settings, then runs the app in local R. Each visitor signs in with their own account and data permissions. You need existing cloud resources; the guide doesn't create them.

Usage

oauth_db_cloud_demo(
  platform = "databricks",
  host = NULL,
  client_id = NULL,
  client_type = NULL,
  warehouse_id = NULL,
  http_path = NULL,
  path = NULL,
  port = NULL,
  edition = NULL,
  action = c("start", "files"),
  prompt = interactive(),
  launch_browser = interactive(),
  ...
)

Arguments

platform

Cloud platform: "databricks", "fabric", "bigquery", "snowflake", "azure-sql", "azure-postgres", "redshift" or "clickhouse".

host

Databricks workspace hostname or browser URL. For other SQL demos, an alias for server.

client_id

Client ID from your custom OAuth app registration.

client_type

"public" for PKCE without a secret, or "confidential". The guide asks when needed; noninteractive calls default to "public" where supported. BigQuery and Snowflake demos use confidential registrations.

warehouse_id

Optional default Databricks SQL warehouse ID.

http_path

Optional Databricks warehouse HTTP path, instead of warehouse_id.

path

Empty or existing cloud-demo directory. The default is a platform-specific directory in R's user cache, so drafts survive restarting R. Existing settings and app edits are preserved. Use a new empty path for a separate setup or fresh templates.

port

Local Shiny port, default 8100 or the saved setting. Register http://localhost:<port> exactly as the OAuth callback.

edition

Databricks only: "workspace", "trial", "free", or "unknown". Free Edition lacks the account-level custom registration this example needs.

action

"start" guides setup and runs the app; "files" writes an editable draft without network calls or asking for a secret.

prompt

Ask interactively for missing settings. Use FALSE in scripts.

launch_browser

Open the local app in a regular browser.

...

Named settings for the selected platform, listed below under Platform settings. Interactive setup asks for missing values.

Value

Invisibly, the demo directory, including after pausing incomplete interactive setup. Noninteractive starts report missing settings as errors.

Details

Run this from an R console to get prompts for missing settings. Sign in through the browser, then click Run example query in the app. Queries use the platform's normal compute or query allowance. Stopping the app doesn't stop shared cloud services or cancel submitted jobs.

All demos need mirai 2.5.1 or later, bslib and processx; install askpass for masked secret input. Databricks also needs brickster 0.2.14 or later and jsonlite. Fabric needs fabricQueryR, odbc and Microsoft ODBC Driver 18. BigQuery and ClickHouse use jsonlite without a database driver. Snowflake, Azure SQL and Redshift need odbc and their native drivers; Azure PostgreSQL needs RPostgres and a trusted CA bundle.

Platform settings

Databricks uses the named arguments above. For other platforms, pass these settings through ...:

Fabric

server, database, tenant_id; optional driver.

BigQuery

project; optional location, maximum_bytes_billed.

Snowflake

server, role, warehouse; optional database, schema, driver.

Azure SQL

server, database, tenant_id; optional driver, database_port.

Azure PostgreSQL

server, database, user, sslrootcert, tenant_id; optional database_port.

Redshift

identity_center_ready, server, database, tenant_id, resource, scope; optional driver, database_port.

ClickHouse

jwt_ready, url, tenant_id, resource, scope; optional database.

database_port is the database's port; port is the local Shiny port. The Redshift and ClickHouse demos use Entra and need an existing trusted-token integration. See the source guide for registration steps.

Edit and resume

The launcher saves non-secret settings in settings.dcf and keeps your app.R edits. Call it again with the same path to resume. Use action = "files" for an offline draft, or a new empty path for fresh templates. For scripts, supply the required settings and prompt = FALSE.

Enter secrets through the masked prompt or the platform's client-secret environment variable. Databricks uses OAUTHDB_DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET; other names are in the source guides. Secrets pass through the app process environment and aren't written to generated files.

Databricks registration

Databricks needs an account-level custom OAuth registration with SQL access and the exact callback URI. Public registrations use PKCE without a secret; confidential registrations need a secret. Free Edition doesn't provide this registration path. After sign-in, select a warehouse or supply its ID manually. See the Databricks vignette for setup.

See also

oauth_db_demo(), oauth_db_databricks_client(), oauth_db_databricks(), oauth_db_databricks_api().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
oauth_db_cloud_demo("databricks")
oauth_db_cloud_demo("fabric")
oauth_db_cloud_demo("bigquery", action = "files", path = "my-bigquery-demo")
path <- oauth_db_cloud_demo("databricks", action = "files", prompt = FALSE)
file.edit(file.path(path, "app.R"))
oauth_db_cloud_demo("databricks", path = path)
} # }
